title: Electric Cell-substrate Impedance Sensing for the Quantification of Endothelial Proliferation, Barrier Function, and Motility
protocol: Prewarm the array holder in an incubator to 37°C before starting the experiment to prevent condensation.
Fill water casket of the incubator with distilled water to avoid drying of the wells.
Perform all manipulations on cells and arrays in a laminar flow cabinet under sterile conditions.
Clean and stabilize ECIS arrays before an experiment.
Add 200 µl/well 10 mM L-cysteine for electrode cleaning and modification.
Incubate with L-cysteine for 15 min at room temperature (RT).
Wash twice with 500 µl/well ultra-pure water.
Coat with 200 µl/well warm 1% gelatin.
Incubate coated arrays in gelatin for 30 min at 37°C.
Remove gelatin without letting surface dry to avoid electrode damage.
Wash once with ultra-pure water (type 1).
Add 400 μl of complete cell culture medium per well.
Place the slide array into the array holder and ensure that the nine gold square pads are properly contacted by the spring-loaded pogo pins.
Tighten the adjustment screw hand tight.
Open the measurement software and press Setup followed by Check in the "Collect Data" section to perform a quick impedance measurement of each individual well.
Verify the selected arrays in the "Well Configuration" section.
Remove array from holder.
Seed cells as a single cell suspension in 400 μl of complete cell culture medium per well.
Add 200 μl/well of complete medium to each well and place the array in the array holder.
Open measurement software and press Setup followed by Check to ascertain the array is properly connected and to measure initial Z, R, and C.
Press Stabilize in the "Collect Data" section to clean the electrodes with a high current (ca. 3 mA), high frequency (64 kHz) pulse.
Check electrodes again after stabilization.
Select the wells to be measured in the "Well Configuration" section.
Verify the selected arrays in the "Well Configuration" section.
Select the measurement mode from the "Collect Data" options.
Select Single Freq. / Time (SFT) from the drop down menu.
Choose the measurement frequency.
Select Multiple Freq. / Time (MFT) for electrode coverage and modeling.
Measure automatically at all available frequencies.
Select Rapid Time Collect (RTC) for micromotion measurements.
Adjust measurement frequency and sampling frequency in RTC mode.
Specify a single well to measure in RTC mode.
Go to Help > Show expert toolbar/menu items > Acquire > Multi-Well RTC if measuring micromotion in several wells subsequently.
Specify the Time limit (hr) in the Collect Data section for Multi-Well RTC.
Enter the value for how often the measurement needs to be repeated after starting the measurement.
Select the time interval between measurements for SFT or leave unchecked for fastest acquisition rate.
Press Start, name the file and select location to store the data.
Stop run by pressing Finish.
Press Pause to stop data acquisition but continue experimental clock.
Remove the array from the holder under laminar flow bench.
Change medium on the array.
Place array back in the holder.
Click Check Connection or Resume Experiment to continue data acquisition.
Mark time in dataset for manipulation events.
Manipulate cells during data acquisition for immediate changes when sterility is not required.
Add the stimulus directly to the well.
Mix carefully with a 200 µl pipette.
Mark the time point manually by pressing Mark.
Add a comment.
Enable Wound / Electroporate Setup.
Click Wound and fill in the time (sec).
Fill in the wound voltage (V for 1,600 R) or current (µA for Z and Z-Theta).
Enter the frequency (Hz).
Select the wells to wound in the "Well Configuration" section.
Check only the wells that will be wounded.
Enable Delay Until Hour and fill in the delay time to activate the delay wound function.
Press Activate and click OK in the pop-up window to start wounding.
Ensure the resistance signal drops to the offset impedance after wounding.
Repeat the wounding if the signal does not drop correctly.
Finish measurement or load data set via File -> Open.
Select wells to be displayed from the "Well Configuration" window.
Group individual wells to present the average.
Choose parameter to be displayed from the upper toolbar (Z, R or C).
Select graph type from the upper toolbar (T = time, F = frequency, 3D = waterfall blot).
Define graph offset and range with the sliders below the graph window or fill in exact values in the adjacent controls.
Perform standard deviation, running average or normalization of the data using "Time-Series Options" in the "Analyze" section.
Activate Expert Toolbar in the Help menu for advanced operations like Nyquist plot and Fourier transformation.
Define range of x- and y-axes and export graph using "Display Options" in the "Analyze" section.
Export selected data to an Excel file via File -> Export Data -> To Excel (Selected).
Use a third-party software of choice for in-depth analysis, statistics, and representation as needed.
If a cell-free reference well is available, press Find to automatically select the reference value or Set to manually select from "Freq. Scan Modeling" in the "Analyzing" section.
Import a reference value from another data set if no cell-free reference is available.
Open the reference data set and use Find or Set to select the reference value.
Navigate to the measured data and press Get to retrieve the values.
Use Model to start calculations if there is no cell-free reference data set, using factory default settings.
Normalize the data set by the averaged resistance of the entire period.
Break the data set into segments with a length of 256-data points.
Clean each segment by applying a Hanning window.
Run a 256-point Fourier transformation on each segment.
Average resulting frequency spectra to a single-sided 129-point power spectrum.
Plot frequency against amplitude in a log-log graph.
Apply least square linear fit to the plotted data.
The slope of the linear fit measures overall noise and micromotion of cells.
